page: Microsoft Azure E104ids_v5 is an isolated, local disk-enabled server instance belonging to the EIDSv5 family. It is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz, featuring 52 physical cores and 104 vCPUs via hyper-threading. The system is equipped with 672.0 GB of RAM, providing 6.46 GB of memory per core, and includes 3891 GB of local SSD storage. The underlying virtualization is managed by Microsoft Hyper-V.

In benchmark evaluations, the E104ids_v5 demonstrates strong multi-core performance, as evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core score of 100,881.58 and a Passmark CPU score of 78,384.05. Single-core performance is moderate, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1,708.0. Memory subsystem performance is highly robust, showing a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 5,422.71 GB/sec and a large block uncached write bandwidth of 139.57 GB/sec. Cryptographic capabilities are exceptional, with the Passmark CPU encryption test achieving a top-tier score of 92,867.76, aided by hardware-accelerated instruction sets like AVX-512 and VAES.

From a resource density perspective, the E104ids_v5 offers a high-capacity memory footprint combined with substantial local SSD storage, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for workloads requiring large in-memory datasets without the overhead of external storage latency. The combination of strong multi-threaded processing, high memory bandwidth, and rapid local SSD storage makes this server well-suited for large-scale database operations, high-throughput web serving, software compilation, and memory-intensive enterprise applications.
